solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flask makes a come-back

definitions.meaning: a glass vessel with a long bent neck used in a chemistry laboratory for distilling
a sharp or witty reply to someone's remark

explanation.surface: A drinks flask is staging a return, like a fashion revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' is only a link joining the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a long-necked distilling vessel in chemistry and a quick sharp reply.

clue.text: Round Australia drink and fruit lifted author

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read from bottom to top
the first word goes round the second

parts.note: ale is beer
Oz is the informal name for Australia
a lime is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A drink and fruit raised in a toast round Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' in a down clue means the whole string is read upwards; 'Round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The French novelist who wrote Germinal and the open letter J'accuse.

clue.text: Two features of cricket take too long

definitions.meaning: an over (six balls) and a run (a point scored) are two cricket terms which together make the word
to exceed a set time limit

explanation.surface: A cricket match dragging on past its time.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries by one bowler and a run is a single point scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on beyond a set time limit, as a meeting or match can.

clue.text: Mass of rock coming from left?

parts.note: something coming from the left is heading towards the right side, and R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A boulder rolling in from the left side.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: split the answer as TO R and it reads 'to right' (R is right), the direction of something coming from the left; 'coming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocky peak or outcrop on a hill, common on Dartmoor in south-west England.

clue.text: Speak badly of wound one can't directly see?

definitions.meaning: to slander someone behind their back
a bite placed on the back, a spot you cannot look at without a mirror

explanation.surface: Gossiping about someone is like an injury inflicted out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic hint: a bite (wound) on the back, where you cannot see it yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander an absent person is a long-standing verb for malicious talk behind their back.

clue.text: Big beast thus disposed of?

parts.note: thus is SO, and putting it in the BIN is having it disposed of

explanation.surface: A huge animal has been got rid of, as if culled.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: SO (thus) inside BIN gives the answer, and 'thus' in the bin is 'thus disposed of'; 'of' rounds off the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A large shaggy wild ox of the North American plains, certainly a big beast.

clue.text: Suck up spicy taste, not liked initially

parts.note: curry is a spicy dish

indicators.note: not means the letter is left out of the word

parts.note: flavour is taste

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone sniffing at a hot dish whose flavour they never liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suck up' looks like slurping food, but it means fawning. 'not ... initially' removes L from FLAVOUR to give FAVOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingratiate yourself with someone by flattery, the idiom for toadying.

clue.text: Love to interrupt endlessly stroppy dancers

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the middle of the other word
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: bolshie is British slang for awkward or rebellious
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Romance breaks out among a troupe of bad-tempered dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BOLSHIE to BOLSHI, and O goes in. 'Stroppy' and 'bolshie' are British slang for bad-tempered and uncooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolshoi Ballet of Moscow is a famous company of ballet dancers.

clue.text: Box tree, in part

definitions.meaning: the main stem of a tree, part of the whole

explanation.surface: A box tree, or a part of one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the box tree; the two senses are a storage chest and the main stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A large storage chest for luggage, and also the woody main stem of a tree.

clue.text: No science subjects mean breaking into so much laughter

indicators.note: one word is broken open so another can sit inside it

parts.note: fits of laughter: so much laughing that you have fits
near means stingy or mean with money

explanation.surface: A student avoiding science finds the average subject merely laughable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' suggests average, but here it is NEAR in the sense of tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, sculpture and music are creative disciplines, the opposite end of the curriculum from physics or chemistry.

clue.text: To assemble is a fag

definitions.meaning: to gather or turn up, as in people rolling up to a meeting
fag is British slang for a cigarette; a hand-rolled one has this name

explanation.surface: Putting something together turns out to be a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. 'Fag' is everyday British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means arrive or gather, and the noun is a cigarette made by hand from loose tobacco.

clue.text: Sorcery may concern criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Witchcraft might be a matter for the criminal courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Black magic that summons the dead is a branch of sorcery.

clue.text: Religious drama; suggesting calmer one?

parts.note: rearrange (play with) the letters of MIRACLE and you get CALMER plus I, which is one

explanation.surface: A sacred drama that seems to suggest someone more serene.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: PLAY works as the anagram signal on MIRACLE, giving CALMER I, and I is 'one'; 'suggesting' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval stage play presenting saints' lives or Bible stories.

clue.text: Long journey that may encounter a hitch?

definitions.text: Long journey that may encounter a hitch?

parts.words: Long journey that may encounter a hitch?
parts.note: a long walk; a hitch is a snag, but put the word 'hitch' before it and you get thumbing lifts by the roadside

explanation.surface: A long trip that might run into problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hitch' looks like a snag, but it points to hitch-hiking.
explanation.definitionFit: A long walk in the countryside, the word that follows hitch in the phrase for thumbing lifts.

clue.text: This time holding run, coming back exhausted

indicators.note: coming back means the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction
one word holds another inside it

parts.note: this time is now, the present moment
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out after jogging back today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts R inside NOW to give NROW; 'coming back' then turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired out or used up: both senses of shabby, threadbare and fatigued fit.

clue.text: Music to make nanny's companion seriously disturbed?

definitions.text: Music to make nanny's companion seriously disturbed?

parts.words: Music to make nanny's companion seriously disturbed?
parts.note: music that would rock (badly shake) a billy, the male goat that keeps a nanny goat company

explanation.surface: Some music is so loud it would upset a goat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nanny' suggests a children's nurse, but it is a female goat, and her companion is the billy; to rock a billy is to disturb him seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: An early style of rock and roll blending country, or hillbilly, music with rhythm and blues.

clue.text: X, cold greeting

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A kiss given with a frosty hello.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like a kiss or a cross, but it is the Greek letter written as X.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet is written with the X shape.

clue.text: With frequency an old don drifts into sleep

indicators.note: drifting suggests the letters wander about into a new order

explanation.surface: An elderly academic often nods off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifts' rearranges F and AN OLD DON together.
explanation.definitionFit: The land of Nod is a jokey idiom for the state of being asleep.

clue.text: Gangster invites in composer briefly for a drink

indicators.note: the first word takes the second inside it, as a host invites a guest in

parts.note: a capo is a Mafia boss

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Puccini wrote the operas La Boheme and Tosca

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss has an opera composer over for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian coffee made with espresso and frothed steamed milk.

clue.text: Moving quietly, preparing cell for raver?

definitions.meaning: lining a cell with soft material, as in the padded cell for someone raving mad

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes about while getting a room ready for a party animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raver' suggests a party-goer, but here means someone who is raving mad.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk with soft steps, and also to line a room with cushioning, as in a padded cell.

clue.text: Pierce page with what one is writing with?

parts.note: ink is what a pen writes with

explanation.surface: Stabbing a sheet of paper with your pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pierce' is an old verb: to prick or stab, as in pinking shears.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb meaning to stab or prick holes in, surviving in pinking shears.

clue.text: Foreign banker puts a lot of money on old computer

parts.note: a pot is a large sum, as in pots of money
a Mac is an Apple computer

explanation.surface: An overseas financier bets heavily on an ageing computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a financier but a river, something with banks; this one is in the USA, foreign to a British solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing past Washington DC is a banker in crossword slang, and abroad.

clue.text: Supply daughter with entertainment

parts.note: fun is amusement or entertainment

explanation.surface: A parent providing their daughter with amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; the order is set by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To finance something is to supply the money it needs.

clue.text: Extremely foul tramp's lost outside

indicators.note: the outer letters of the words are lost, leaving the inside letters

explanation.surface: A dirty vagrant has wandered off outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the outside letters of FOUL TRAMP and what is left inside spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: As a prefix or adverb it means beyond or excessively, as in ultra-modern.

clue.text: Coming to an end of atonement, assuming the lead in reparations

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the long word takes the letter into itself

parts.note: expiation is atonement for sin or wrongdoing

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An act of contrition that ends with someone taking charge of compensation payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Running out or terminating, as a passport or contract does on its last date.

clue.text: Liable for flat

definitions.meaning: lying face down, stretched out on the ground

explanation.surface: Likely to need a home, a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined to something, and also lying face downwards on the ground.

clue.text: How you choose a fabric …

parts.note: twill is a woven fabric with diagonal ridges

explanation.surface: Picking out a cloth, as the ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to the next one for the surface only: 'how you choose a fabric … no bias'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as you please, freely and whenever you like.

clue.text: … no bias, please write with care

parts.note: O is an exclamation used to open a plea, as in 'O grant me...'
to pen is to write
to mind is to care or look after

explanation.surface: Carrying on from the last clue, fabric cut without a bias, and a request to write neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: In sewing, cloth is cut on the bias, which the surface uses; here bias is prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom from prejudice: a willingness to consider ideas without having already decided.

clue.text: Heard song before in poem

indicators.note: heard means the word is said aloud and its sound gives the answer's spelling

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A song was heard before it appeared in a poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, air sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic and archaic word for before, found in verse.

clue.text: Swill round, swallowing only in extremis? That's grotesque

indicators.note: the first word swallows the second, taking it inside

parts.note: to gargle is to swill liquid round the throat

indicators.note: in extremis means at the extremes, so the word's first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: Swishing liquid round the mouth and just swallowing in an emergency is grotesque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a link. 'grotesque' is a noun here: a carved grotesque figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved stone spout of a monstrous face on a church roof is a classic grotesque.

clue.text: Make incomprehensible poem after being regularly crazy in the head

indicators.note: after means the poem comes after the other letters
regularly means every second letter of the word is taken
the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Writing a poem after going regularly mad makes it unreadable.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a message into cipher so outsiders cannot read it.
